meta.subtitle: Edge AI and Industrial IoT maker turning toward unmanned-systems compute; net cash and positive free cash flow, still GAAP loss-making.

analystCommentary: Our call on Lantronix is BUY. The case is a turnaround that shows in the quarters but not yet in the full year: the fourth quarter of FY26 extended a run of sequential revenue growth and gross margin rose, while the annual GAAP result remained a loss, as the risks section sets out. Unmanned-systems compute is the new engine and the Nero Global Tracking acquisition adds recurring revenue; the growth section weighs both. The balance sheet carries no debt, so the shift does not depend on outside financing. The valuation turns on one judgment: whether the market still pays today's forward earnings multiple a year from now on the Street's EPS path. Our Base says it does; our Bear returns the stock to its 52-week low. The final recommendation explains why we publish one notch below the label our scenarios derive.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Lantronix, Inc., incorporated in 1989 and headquartered in Irvine, California, develops and sells industrial and enterprise Internet of Things (IoT) products and services. The 10-K's MD&A organizes the portfolio into three product lines: Embedded IoT Solutions, IoT Systems Solutions, and Software and Services. Embedded products include compute system-on-module and system-in-package solutions for applications such as computer vision and machine learning. IoT Systems Solutions cover routing, switching and gateway functions, telematics, media conversion, and wired and wireless connectivity, including power over Ethernet. Software and services include out-of-band management, GPS-based vehicle and asset tracking, engineering services, and extended warranty and support. The company describes itself as a provider of Edge AI and Industrial IoT solutions that power NDAA-compliant unmanned systems, critical infrastructure and resilient enterprise networks. It manages its sales teams by three geographic regions: the Americas, EMEA, and APJ.

thesis.body: The stock trades at $6.25, below the bottom of the Street's target range, while the business has turned on a quarterly basis and gained a new growth line in unmanned-systems compute. A debt-free balance sheet removes financing risk from the turn. Our Base case needs no re-rating on earnings: it holds today's forward multiple a year out on the Street's EPS path. The case against is that the turn is not yet visible in the full-year GAAP numbers and that the EPS path the Base rests on carries no GAAP or non-GAAP label in the pack.

catalysts: Results for the September 2026 quarter are an early test of the Q1 FY2027 revenue guide and of management's double-digit growth outlook for FY2027.
Progress of unmanned-systems revenue toward the FY2027 share of total revenue that management targets.
The Vecima industrial IoT business closed on August 1, 2026; its purchase accounting and first revenue arrive with the quarter ending September 30, 2026.

A March 2026 U.S. Court of International Trade ruling may entitle the company to refunds of IEEPA-based tariffs it paid; as of June 30, 2026 it had recognized no amount, and the timing and extent remain uncertain.
risks: A few distributors and end-user customers account for a large part of revenue.
Unmanned-systems demand depends on customers winning U.S. and allied government contracts.
Single-source integrated circuits and a current memory shortage expose costs and shipments.
The annual numbers have not yet confirmed the quarterly turn; see the execution risk below.

financials.incomeCommentary: FY26 revenue was $120.9M, {- -1.6% -} year over year, after FY25 fell {- -23.3% -} and FY24 rose {+ +22.2% +}. Gross margin rose to 43.8% from 42.1% in FY25, above each of the other four years in the table (42.9%, 42.9% and 40.1% before FY25). Operating margin improved to -3.4% from -8.9% but stayed negative, and the company has posted an operating loss in each of the five years shown. Net income was -$4.2M and GAAP diluted EPS was $-0.10, narrower than $-0.29 in FY25. The company also reported non-GAAP EPS of $0.15 for FY26 and $0.04 for the fourth quarter; its non-GAAP measure excludes share-based compensation, amortization, restructuring and acquisition-related costs among other items. Q4'26 (the quarter ended June 30, 2026) revenue was $31.2M, up 4.6% year over year on the desk's figures; the company's August 26, 2026 release describes the same quarter as up 8%, and we use the 4.6% figure. The CEO called it the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth. The fourth-quarter operating margin was -1.3%, closer to break-even than the full year. The trend is improving at the gross and operating lines, but the year still closed with an operating loss.
financials.balanceCommentary: Lantronix ended FY26 with $60 million in cash and no debt, per the August 26, 2026 earnings release; the desk records net debt of -$60.5M, a net cash position. The current ratio rose to 3.66 from 2.54 a year earlier, above each of the other four years in the table (2.53, 2.08 and 2.95 before FY25). In that release the CEO said the company enters fiscal 2027 in "the strongest financial position in our company's history". The MD&A reports that the fourth-quarter FY26 qualitative goodwill assessment for the company's single reporting unit did not indicate impairment, so no quantitative test was required. Deferred tax assets are fully offset by a valuation allowance, reflecting historical net operating losses and uncertainty about future taxable income; a return to sustained taxable profit could reverse it. The balance sheet is the floor under the case: it funds the Vecima acquisition, closed on August 1, 2026, without borrowing, and leaves room to absorb a slower year.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow was $9.3M in FY26, a 7.7% FCF margin, and has been positive for three straight years after margins of 10.7% in FY24 and 5.5% in FY25; FY22 and FY23 were negative. Capital expenditure was about $612,000 in FY26, so almost all operating cash flow reached free cash flow. The gap between the FY26 net loss and positive free cash flow is consistent with non-cash charges such as share-based compensation and amortization, which the company excludes from its non-GAAP results. The pack carries no cash-flow bridge from net loss to operating cash flow, though, so working capital may also contribute, and we do not read the non-GAAP exclusion list as a cash reconciliation. Positive free cash flow in a loss-making year is useful, but its quality is unproven until it recurs alongside a GAAP profit.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Trailing multiples say little. The P/E is -62.5x because FY26 was a loss, and EV/EBITDA is not reported in the pack. Price-to-sales is 2.4x. The forward P/E on the next twelve months is 27.0x, close to the price over FY27E consensus EPS of $0.23, so we treat it as the current-year multiple and the like-for-like reference for our scenarios. On FY28E consensus EPS of $0.32 the stock trades at about 19.5x. The pack does not label the consensus EPS as GAAP or non-GAAP; it sits much closer to the company's $0.15 non-GAAP FY26 EPS than to its GAAP loss, so we treat the earnings anchor with caution. The trailing free cash flow yield is 3.2%, so the shares are not cheap on cash today; the case rests on earnings growth. No peer multiples are available, so we make no premium or discount claim. All six analysts rate the stock Buy, with targets at a consensus of $10.25, a median of $10.50 and a range of $8.00 to $12.00. With no dissent on the Street, we use the high target only as the Bull anchor and build the Base from multiples instead.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Unmanned systems reaches the top of management's FY2027 revenue-share range, revenue and EPS run ahead of consensus, and the market pays more than today's forward P/E on the higher earnings. Anchor: the Street's $12.00 high target. It sits above the $8.75 52-week high and needs an earnings beat and a re-rating together.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue reaches the FY27E consensus and the Street's EPS path holds. A year out, the market keeps today's 27.0x forward P/E and applies it to FY28E consensus EPS of $0.32: the same multiple rolled forward one year, not a re-rating. The anchor is consensus EPS whose GAAP or non-GAAP basis the pack does not label.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Customer concentration, component shortages or defense-budget timing stall the turn: organic revenue falls enough to offset the acquired business, GAAP losses persist, and the Street's EPS path is cut. The stock returns to its $4.37 52-week low, a price the market paid within the past year; on flat revenue that is a sales multiple well below today's 2.4x.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The scenarios weight to a fair value of $8.24. Expected upside is +31.9%, bear-case downside is -30.1%, and reward/risk is 1.06x, which derives STRONG BUY, just over the 1.00x bar.

**The multiple.** For holding today's forward multiple a year out: consensus has revenue and EPS rising again into FY28E, so the growth that supports a high forward multiple today is still modelled a year later. Against it: that multiple sits on EPS of unlabelled basis while the GAAP result is a loss; the trailing free cash flow yield gives no cash support at a higher price; and on sales the Base needs a clearly higher sales multiple than today's, because consensus has earnings growing much faster than revenue. The Base is a bet that the margin expansion consensus models arrives, and that anchor decides the label.

**The weights.** Bull gets 20% because it needs an earnings beat and a re-rating at once, at a price the stock has not reached in the past year. Base gets 55% because the sequential run, unmanned revenue above the midpoint of its outlook and the closed acquisition all point toward the consensus path. Bear gets 25%. It needs organic revenue to shrink after five quarters of sequential growth, which is why it is not the likeliest case; but FY25 showed how fast revenue can fall, and the low end of the Q1 guide sits below Q4'26 revenue, so it is not a tail. We set the Bear at the 52-week low, not above it, because its conditions are no better than those under which the market paid that price. We do not set it below, because the Bear keeps the net cash and positive free cash flow; a deeper fall is a tail rather than the Bear.

**Sensitivity.** Toward caution, moving five points from Base to Bear, or swapping the earnings anchor for today's sales multiple on FY27E revenue, takes reward/risk below that bar and derives BUY. Only a Base near today's price would derive HOLD. Toward optimism, moving five points from Base to Bull keeps STRONG BUY with more room.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The pack shows Lantronix as a single reportable segment and carries no product or geographic revenue split, so FY26 revenue of $120.9M appears as one consolidated line. The MD&A names three product lines (Embedded IoT Solutions, IoT Systems Solutions, and Software and Services) and three sales regions, but the pack gives no revenue by line or region. In the August 26, 2026 release the CEO framed the business around three strategic focus areas: unmanned systems, critical infrastructure, and enterprise networking. Without a split, the report cannot show which line earns the improved gross margin.

moatFactors.name: Embedded design-in stickiness
moatFactors.body: System-on-module and system-in-package products are designed into customer platforms, which can raise switching costs once a customer qualifies a part. The benefit is narrow because it rests on a small group of large customers, the concentration risk set out in the risks section.

moatFactors.name: Certification and compliance
moatFactors.body: The company positions its compute for NDAA-compliant unmanned systems and offers pre-certified products. Compliance requirements can narrow the field of qualified suppliers for defense and critical-infrastructure buyers, but the edge is early and the pack carries no figure that shows it in margins.

moatFactors.name: Pricing power
moatFactors.body: The forward-looking statements in the August 26, 2026 earnings release list "intense competition in our industry and resultant downward price pressure" among the factors that could affect results. An operating loss in each of the last five years points the same way, despite the gross-margin gain.

moatFactors.name: Scale
moatFactors.body: The 10-K's risk factors say that, due to the company's limited sales, it may not be able to convince suppliers to keep making components available unless other customers also demand them. That is the opposite of a scale advantage.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NONE. Of the four factors, the two that could build durability, design-ins and compliance, are modest or early, and the two that would show it in the numbers, pricing power and scale, are weak. What would change the rating is evidence in the reported results: an operating margin that turns and stays positive while gross margin holds, and a rising share of recurring Software and Services revenue that the Nero acquisition is expected to lift. Until then any advantage is prospective. The net-cash balance sheet buys time to prove it, but time is not a moat.

points: Consensus models FY27E revenue of $138.6M, in line with management's double-digit growth outlook, and revenue rising again to $157.2M in FY28E.

Unmanned systems revenue was $12.6M in FY26, from a minimal contribution in FY25 and above the midpoint of the company's $10 million to $14 million outlook. Active engagements rose to more than 30 from about 10 during the year, and management expects the business to be 15% to 20% of FY2027 revenue. Partnerships with Swarmer, DoD Solution and AVT Australia place the company's system-on-module technology in drone and payload programs. The beat on its own outlook is the strongest evidence in the pack that the new engine is real.

The Nero Global Tracking acquisition is expected to add about $5.3 million of annual revenue, including about $4.5 million of ARR and about 125,000 asset tags under management, and lifts Software and Services above 10% of revenue on a pro forma basis. It shifts the mix toward recurring revenue more than it moves the total.

The SLC 9000 out-of-band console manager, integrated with Percepxion, targets the AI data center networking market; the pack has no revenue figure for it, so it is an option rather than a driver of our numbers.

The Q1 FY2027 guide is revenue of $31.0 million to $33.0 million, against $31.2M in Q4'26. The midpoint implies another sequential gain, but the guide alone does not show a double-digit year: that needs further sequential growth through FY2027 on top of the acquired revenue, and the pack has no Q1 FY26 revenue to read the guide year over year.

Three readings cut the other way. The low end of that guide sits below Q4'26 revenue, so a sixth straight sequential gain is not assured; the acquired revenue is small against FY26 revenue of $120.9M, so most of the growth consensus models must be organic; and the unmanned ramp carries the government-contract risk set out in the risks section.

management.leadership: Saleel Awsare is president and chief executive officer. The DEF 14A filed September 24, 2025 listed him as a director, with James Auker, Sailesh Chittipeddi and Hoshi Printer as directors and Narbeh Derhacobian and Kevin Palatnik as director nominees for that year's meeting; it named Mathi Gurusamy as Chief Product & Strategy Officer and Kurt Hoff as Chief Revenue Officer. The pack does not show whether the roster has changed since. In the August 26, 2026 release Mr. Awsare set out a strategy of transforming Lantronix from a broad-based hardware provider into a more focused, higher-margin solutions platform. FY26 shows partial delivery: unmanned-systems revenue beat the outlook management had given, and gross margin rose, but the operating line has not yet followed. We judge the strategy coherent and the early execution credible, with the operating result still to prove.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation has favored the balance sheet and targeted M&A. The dividend yield is 0.00%, and the pack reports no share repurchases in any of the five years shown. In August 2026 the company used about $11.7 million, excluding working capital and other customary adjustments, to buy Vecima Networks' industrial IoT business, including the Nero Global Tracking platform. The MD&A says the purchase price allocation, including goodwill and intangible assets, will be disclosed for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The deal is small against the company's cash and buys recurring revenue in an adjacent tracking market, which fits the stated strategy. We view the allocation as disciplined; the test is whether the acquired business adds to profit, which the pack cannot yet show.
management.governance: Governance disclosures rest on the DEF 14A filed September 24, 2025, now about a year old. That proxy reports no related-person transactions requiring disclosure during fiscal 2025 or 2024, and none proposed. The company indemnifies its directors and officers to the fullest extent permitted by law and has indemnification agreements with each of them. The proxy's ownership percentages are measured against 39,271,361 shares outstanding as of September 8, 2025. The pack's current share count, about 46.71M and derived from market cap, is above that base, so the proxy's percentages may overstate holders' current stakes. The excerpt carries no board-independence or compensation detail, so we draw no conclusion on either. On what is disclosed, we see no governance red flag.
management.insiderOwnership: As of September 8, 2025, per the proxy, Bernhard Bruscha beneficially owned 13.8% (5,423,357 shares, of which 5,166,471 were held through TL Investment GmbH, where he is managing director), and Chain of Lakes Group held 7.8% (3,072,343 shares), based on a Schedule 13D/A filed July 1, 2025. Mr. Awsare held 1.1% (447,960 shares), and all current executive officers and directors as a group, nine persons, held 2.4% (951,464 shares). A holder of that size has a large block, not control, but on any contested vote it carries weight that outside holders should track. The two outside blocks together are far larger than the board and management's combined stake, so the swing votes sit with outside investors rather than insiders. Insider ownership is modest, and the pack carries no pay detail, so we cannot say how management's incentives are aligned with shareholders.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration: the 10-K says the company has relied on a small number of distributors and end-user customers for a significant portion of net revenue, and the loss of one, or a decline in their orders, could cause a material loss of sales and excess inventory.

Government and defense exposure: the 10-K says growth in drone and defense markets depends on customers winning government contracts, in particular from the U.S. Department of War. Those programs depend on appropriations, can be cut by budget reductions or shutdowns, and can be terminated for convenience, which makes the timing of these sales unpredictable.

Supply chain and manufacturing: some integrated circuits are single-sourced or no longer made, the market is experiencing memory shortages that raise costs, and the company has at times been unable to fill orders for lack of components. It has no long-term supply arrangements with most vendors, and contract manufacturers in Asia make substantially all of its products without guaranteed supply agreements.

Execution on the turn: FY26 revenue was still down 1.6% and the company remained GAAP loss-making, with EPS of $-0.10, so the shift toward unmanned systems and higher-margin software has yet to show in a full year. Integrating the Nero Global Tracking business adds execution risk at the same time.
Tariffs: the company has paid IEEPA-based tariffs; any refund after the March 2026 court ruling is uncertain in timing and extent, and future tariff changes could raise costs.
risks.systemic: The 10-K's risk factors tie component shortages and price swings to a pandemic or epidemic, the war between Ukraine and Russia, conflict in the Middle East, hostilities in the Red Sea, tensions between China and Taiwan, and increased tariffs and changes in U.S. trade policy. Separately, the forward-looking statements in the August 26, 2026 earnings release name negative or worsening regional and worldwide economic conditions and their effect on customer purchasing decisions, the impact of rising interest rates, and the stability of the company's financial and banking institutions. With a $291.9M market cap and an earnings recovery still ahead, the shares are also exposed to shifts in investor appetite for small companies that have not yet turned a GAAP profit.

body: We rate Lantronix a BUY with a target range of $8.00 to $10.00 against a $6.25 price. Our scenarios derive STRONG BUY, with expected upside of +31.9% and reward/risk of 1.06x; we publish BUY as a deliberate one-notch-conservative call. The reward/risk clears the 1.00x bar narrowly, and the sensitivity in the valuation section shows that either of two defensible changes, five points of weight from Base to Bear or a sales anchor in place of the earnings anchor, derives BUY. The Base also rests on consensus EPS of unlabelled basis while the GAAP result is still a loss. BUY is the label that holds under both readings.

We would move to STRONG BUY on a reported quarter with a positive GAAP operating margin while revenue tracks the FY27E consensus, because that would confirm the earnings path the Base assumes. We would move toward HOLD if a quarter lands below the low end of the Q1 FY2027 revenue guide or management lowers its unmanned-systems revenue-share outlook, because either would raise the Bear weight and cut the Base.
